name: @odu/launch
//cordis: THE ROW this package belongs to, read by the fence. A row is a capability the daemon serves — `ci` for the runs and the machinery around them, `cache` for the buckets. This package is in `ci` because a face needs it to converge on the singleton; `@odu/host` is the roster and belongs to no row, which is what lets it name them all.
//: HOW A CLIENT CONVERGES ON THE SINGLETON — the launch facts, the gate's identity reader, and adopt/spawn/refuse. See README.md. It names no ROW: a row may import it (a face on a cold machine has to start the service it cannot find), and so may the root that composes the rows. That is the whole reason it is a package of its own rather than a corner of `@odu/host`: the host IS the registry — it names every row — and a row importing the registry is exactly the cycle the fence refuses.
//dependencies: `@odu/service-client` for the contract, its dial and its socket path; `@odu/execution` for the spawn description a daemon is launched with and the one Effect edge; two @kolu daemon packages for the pid gate and the survivable spawn; `osfacts-client` for the gate's process reader. `@odu/host`, `@odu/cli`, `@odu/cache` and `@odu/web-ui` are ABSENT and `src/closure.test.ts` refuses them: this package is what makes rows and the registry able to share one bootstrap.
